mcq.question: What makes Bresenham's line algorithm well suited to drawing pixels?

options.A: It uses floating-point slopes for perfect accuracy
options.B: It draws every pixel in the bounding rectangle
options.C: It decides each next pixel using only integer additions and comparisons

mcq.explanation: Bresenham keeps an integer error term and steps along the major axis, choosing the minor-axis step when the error crosses a threshold. No division or floating point is needed.

mcq.question: Why does `flood_fill` use an explicit `std::vector` as a stack instead of recursion?

options.A: Recursion is not allowed in member functions
options.B: Recursing once per pixel could overflow the call stack for large areas
options.C: Vectors make the fill visit pixels in diagonal order
options.D: The explicit stack fills fewer pixels

mcq.explanation: The call stack is small (often 1–8 MB). An explicit stack lives on the heap and can grow to millions of entries.
